report.summary: The mine’s level 2 upgrade finished, and three contacts are active. No trade or supply action was taken.
report.whatChanged: The receipt confirms mine level 2 completed. The contacts list and consequences show accepted contacts with Sim Farmer 48, Sim Miner 58, and Sim Farmer 78. Five other incoming contact requests still await your acceptance. There are no open supply offers or active supply contracts. No action was rejected, queued, proposed, or signed in the provided receipts.
report.nextDecision: Compare partners once someone shares concrete resource needs or offer terms. You can also decide whether to accept any of the five pending contact requests; those are not active contacts yet.
report.reasonToReturn: Return when you have concrete terms to compare or want to review which incoming contact requests to accept.
report.confusion: The plan says there were no accepted contacts, but the receipts show three accepted contacts are now active. The plan is not the record of what happened; the receipts are.

report.summary: The mine upgrade was accepted and is now being built. It has not finished yet.
report.whatChanged: The receipt confirms the level 2 mine upgrade committed. It charged 50 iron and 25 silver, and the mine is active in builder slot 1 with about 11 game minutes remaining. The mine still shows level 1 because the upgrade is unfinished. Nothing here was rejected, merely proposed, signed, or already finished. Three contacts are accepted; five incoming contact requests are waiting for the human controller to decide. There are no open supply offers or active supply contracts.
report.nextDecision: Wait for the mine upgrade to finish, then review the new state before choosing another action. The other builder slot is free, but the mine itself is busy, so it cannot take another mine upgrade now.
report.reasonToReturn: Return when the mine has finished so you can see its new level and decide what to build next.
report.confusion: The plan expected a 10 minute build, while the actual state reports about 11 game minutes remaining. The receipt and current state confirm it is active, not finished.

report.summary: The farm and mine upgrades are finished. A market upgrade and a message to the merchant were both committed.
report.whatChanged: The market upgrade is queued and active in builder slot 1, with about 11 game minutes remaining. Its receipt confirms that 40 iron and 30 silver were charged. The merchant message was sent successfully. Nothing here shows a proposed or signed supply contract; there are no active supply contracts. Builder slot 2 is idle. The later stock check says no listed upgrade is currently affordable, despite the earlier plan describing the market upgrade as affordable; the successful receipt confirms the upgrade was committed and charged.
report.nextDecision: Wait for the market upgrade to finish, then reassess stock and the merchant's reply before making a trade proposal or signing a contract.
report.reasonToReturn: Return when the market upgrade finishes or the merchant replies, so you can choose the next production or trade step using current information.
report.confusion: The plan said there were no incoming contact requests, but the resulting state lists several incoming requests awaiting your acceptance. Also, the plan said the market upgrade was affordable, while the later stock check marks it unaffordable; the receipt resolves whether it was queued, but not the reason the affordability changed.

report.summary: The farm level 2 upgrade was queued successfully and is now active construction, due in about 11 game minutes. It has not finished yet.
report.whatChanged: The receipt says COMMITTED: 40 iron and 20 silver were charged, and a build record was created. The farm is still level 1 while construction runs; the build will make it level 2 when finished. The kingdom remains active. Grain currently nets 22 whole per hour, but the farm upgrade’s production payoff is not given, so its return cannot yet be calculated. The earlier plan’s claim that both builders were free is contradicted by the receipt and resulting state: slot 1 is now occupied and slot 2 is free. No action was rejected, and nothing here is merely proposed, signed, or queued for supply; the farm build alone is queued and active.
report.nextDecision: Once construction finishes, compare the farm’s new grain rate with current needs before choosing another upgrade. For now, avoid queuing another farm upgrade because that building is busy; a different builder slot does not bypass the restriction.
report.reasonToReturn: Return after the build completes to check the actual production change and decide whether the cost paid off.
report.confusion: The plan described the farm as not busy and both builders as free, but the receipt and after-state show the farm build active in slot 1. The build is not finished yet.

report.summary: You signed Farmer 12’s one-hour offer to exchange 3 grain per hour for 3 iron per hour. The receipt says your signature was committed.
report.whatChanged: The offer remains open as version 1, with your kingdom listed as the only signer. No trade is active yet; there are no active supply contracts, and no deliveries are recorded. Nothing in the receipt says the offer was rejected, queued, or finished. The plan proposed signing, and that signing is now recorded.
report.nextDecision: Wait to see whether Farmer 12 signs the same offer version before its listed expiry. Your signature alone does not start the exchange.
report.reasonToReturn: Return when Farmer 12 signs, the offer expires or changes, or you want to review another concrete trade decision.
report.confusion: The plan says Farmer 12 accepted contact, and the after-state lists Farmer 12 as a contact. But the retained contact consequence shows an earlier acceptance time, so it does not establish a new contact event in this turn. Also, “COMMITTED” confirms your signature was recorded; it does not mean the contract is active.

report.summary: The message to Sim Merchant 53 was committed and recorded. Your kingdom remains active, with about 13.03 ordinary Grain and no signed supply contracts.
report.whatChanged: You sent the merchant a question about quantity and delivery timing, while stating you want to keep a 20-Grain reserve. The receipt confirms the message was committed; it does not confirm a reply or agreement. The planned message was not rejected or merely queued. No trade was proposed or signed, and no new contract became active. The supplied state also shows three accepted contacts and five incoming contact requests awaiting your decision. The completed farm upgrade is recorded separately in the consequences.
report.nextDecision: Wait for a reply and for Grain to recover before considering any supply terms. Review the five incoming contact requests yourself; they require your acceptance.
report.reasonToReturn: Return when the merchant replies or your Grain stock rises past 20 whole, so you can judge concrete terms against your reserve.
report.confusion: The plan says Grain is recovering at 37 whole per hour, but the supplied snapshot gives no recovery estimate or wait duration. Its stated Grain floor is 20, while the rules also give a reserve floor of 12,000 marked units (20 whole).

report.summary: The market upgrade is finished, and your message to Sim Miner 04 was sent. No trade is signed or active.
report.whatChanged: The receipt confirms the message was committed. It opens a discussion about a possible one-hour, no-bond grain-for-iron trade, but it does not create a trade offer or contract. The market is level 2 and completed; the mine is also level 2 and completed. One offer from Sim Miner 34 is still open and unsigned: you would send 3 silver per hour and receive 3 iron per hour for one hour. No supply contract is active. Four incoming contact requests are awaiting your acceptance.
report.nextDecision: Wait for Sim Miner 04’s reply, then check current resources and authority before deciding whether to sign any feasible offer. The market and mine level 3 upgrades are not affordable from current stock; the barracks, farm, storehouse, and wall level 2 upgrades are marked affordable.
report.reasonToReturn: Return when Sim Miner 04 replies or before the open Sim Miner 34 offer expires, so you can review the terms and choose whether to sign.
report.confusion: The plan says the mandate does not allow supply offers or counters, but the provided mandate lists supply.sign as allowed. That permission does not make the existing offer signed: its signedBy list is empty. The message receipt outranks the plan and confirms the message was sent.

report.summary: Your message to Sim Miner 85 was committed and recorded. You asked what resource they need and floated the idea of a small one-hour swap without promising anything.
report.whatChanged: The mine upgrade is finished, and both builders are free. The farmer's offer to exchange 3 iron/hour for 3 grain/hour is still open and unsigned by either side; a second, similar farmer offer has only the farmer's signature. There are no active supply contracts. Three contact requests are waiting for your decision. Your plan's claim that building.queue is not allowed is contradicted by the current mandate, which lists it as allowed.
report.nextDecision: Wait for Sim Miner 85's reply and decide whether to accept the three incoming contact requests. You could also consider a building upgrade under the current mandate if stock and construction checks allow it.
report.reasonToReturn: Return when the miner replies or when you want to review the contact requests and open trade offers.
report.confusion: The plan says the farmer offer is signed by the farmer, but the matching offer listed for gsimfarmer7 has signedBy empty. The other farmer offer is signed by gsimfarmer4. Receipt records take precedence for the action taken: the message is committed; no trade or building action was issued.

report.summary: No actions were issued this turn. The market level 2 is finished, both builders are free, and there are no messages, supply offers, or contracts to address. The plan to wait for a concrete trade need remains appropriate.
report.whatChanged: The consequence receipt confirms three building completions: farm level 2, mine level 2, and market level 2. It also records six accepted contacts, including the three contacts the plan said were already accepted. Three other incoming contact requests are still awaiting the human owner's acceptance; they are not accepted contacts. No construction or supply action is queued, proposed, signed, or active. There are no active supply contracts.
report.nextDecision: Wait for a specific trade proposal or request before considering a reciprocal supply commitment. Ordinary stocks are low, and none of the listed next building upgrades is affordable from current stock.
report.reasonToReturn: Return when a neighbour sends a specific trade proposal or request, so you can assess its terms against your reserves.
report.confusion: The plan says all three incoming requests shown in the guide already appear as accepted, but the current receipt lists three incoming requests as still awaiting your acceptance. Receipt truth takes priority; the separate consequences record confirms six accepted contacts, which include the three mentioned in the plan.

report.summary: One message was sent to Sim Farmer 57 asking them to confirm the one-hour trade terms. No trade was signed or started.
report.whatChanged: The send receipt says COMMITTED and confirms the message was recorded. The open offer is version 1: they propose sending 3 grain per hour, and you would send 3 iron per hour, for one hour. It is signed by them only. There are no active supply contracts. Three incoming contact requests still await the owner’s acceptance; none was accepted in this turn. The farm’s level 2 upgrade is finished. The offer is queued/open, not a finished or active trade. No offer was proposed or signed by you.
report.nextDecision: Decide whether to accept the three pending contacts, and whether to sign the offer if its terms remain worthwhile. Your ordinary stocks are about 13.77 grain and 9.33 iron; the trade would commit 3 iron per hour for one hour in exchange for 3 grain per hour.
report.reasonToReturn: Return when Sim Farmer 57 replies or the offer’s one-hour expiry is near, so you can review any clarification and decide whether to sign before it expires.
report.confusion: The plan says the message was sent, and the receipt confirms it was committed; it does not show any reply. The offer remains open and signed only by Sim Farmer 57. “Queued” here means awaiting your decision, not an active contract. The exact expiry is game time 1791147240000.
